title: Owned lifecycle, disposition, and no-orphan residue
problem: Durable temporary resources can outlive a task or process and become orphaned, unsafe, costly, or destructive to evidence when their terminal disposition is unspecified.
invariant: A triggered durable temporary resource has an owner, bounded purpose, lifecycle boundary, evidence-aware terminal disposition, and explicit retention or cleanup basis.
applicability_triggers: A temporary resource is durable across sessions or process boundaries.
The resource is costly, sensitive, externally allocated, or required by evidence or recovery.
non_applicability_triggers: The value is process-local, disposable, and cannot outlive its owning operation.
An existing task, artifact, lease, or operations record already owns the complete lifecycle.
exclusions: No domain residue, inventory, or perishability vocabulary.
No cleanup action without separately valid authority.
required_contracts: Terminal disposition, cleanup basis, and limitations.
prohibited_shortcuts: Treating process exit as proof of cleanup.
Deleting a resource that is still required by evidence or recovery.
Recording every trivial ephemeral value as durable governance state.
failure_recovery_semantics: An expired or ownerless triggered resource is unresolved, not silently clean.
Cleanup failure preserves discoverability and records residual consequences.
Evidence retention overrides cleanup only through an explicit bounded basis.
proof_expectations: Demonstrate the exact durable resource and lifecycle boundary.
Exercise expiry, terminal disposition, orphan detection, and cleanup failure.
Prove cleanup preserves referenced evidence and sensitive-data minimization.
known_implementations: Octon Mini task cancellation, artifact retention, coordination handback, and operations retirement are partial specialized realizations.

evidence.exact_subject: Project Blueprint 3.0.0 task, artifact, lease, Git cleanup, and operations contracts
evidence.supports: Existing specialized lifecycles cover common cases while a generic durable-temporary-resource contract remains optional.
limitations: This architecture review is not an adopting-project proof.
